summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 16% to Rs.239 crores and EBITDA rose 22% to Rs.60 crores at a 25.3% margin; FY27 guidance held.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.239 crores, up 16% YoY, with domestic up 33%, international down 14% on order-execution timing, and fenestration up 82%. EBITDA was Rs.60 crores (25.3% margin, up 138 bps), or 26.9% after stripping out Rs.14 crores of pass-through freight income and expense. Order book stood at Rs.957 crores at September 30, 2026, with management targeting Rs.500 crores-plus of new bookings in Q3-Q4 to hold about 18 months of visibility. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 20-22% and EBITDA margin of 23-25%, and said Q3-Q4 will be stronger.

financial_highlights.change: stated as in the same region as last year
added to both revenue and expenses

segments.name: Domestic (commercial, hospitality, residential, pan-India for Grade A developers)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.140 crores, up 33% YoY. Management says Tier 1 demand is strong and the domestic bid pipeline exceeds Rs.3,000 crores. One or two projects are running behind on the client side, which management does not consider material.

segments.name: International (US, Australia and others)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.76 crores, down 14% YoY on execution timing. Management says existing US jobs are funded and dispatching daily. New US awards are being held back by developers over tariffs, shipping costs and commodity prices, with a couple of awards expected in Q3-Q4. Israel is a new market, with a first job expected below Rs.50 crores.

segments.name: Fenestration / luxury residential
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.22 crores, up 82% YoY, which management said reflects project execution rather than a run-rate. Management expects substantial bookings in Q3-Q4 and says the segment carries higher margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-22%, unchanged from the previous call.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23-25% and PAT margin at 18-20%, both unchanged.
Q3-Q4 expected to be much stronger; an analyst extrapolation of over 30% H2 top-line growth was described as ballpark accurate by management.
Target of Rs.500 crores-plus of new order bookings in Q3-Q4 to end FY27 with about 18 months of visibility.
Glass processing unit commissioning expected July-August 2027, with an estimated 1-1.5% EBITDA margin benefit from Q3-Q4 FY28.
Working capital days guided at around 45 days, with anything below that described as a bonus.
capex_capacity: Glass processing unit project cost is about Rs.70-odd crores, funded from IPO proceeds held separately. Civil construction is expected to finish in 2-3 months, machinery arrival in 6-7 months, and commissioning in 2-3 months.
Other capex is expected to be no more than Rs.20 crores over the next 1.5-2 years, funded from internal accruals.

Current capacity utilisation is about 55-60%. Management says peak revenue of Rs.1,000-plus crores is achievable from the existing facility without material capex, and that this covers about 4 years of 22% growth.
The company has bought a couple of machines and is evaluating additional machinery for BIPV glass production, which is at R&D stage.
demand_pricing: Order book of Rs.957 crores at September 30, 2026, against Rs.846 crores at April 2026 and Rs.383 crores at the start of FY26. Management expects to execute about Rs.350 crores over the next two quarters and says the book will run for 18-24 months.

Average order size is now Rs.60-70 crores, with Rs.80-100 crores jobs described as normal. Bids include a Rs.400 crore Mumbai job, a Rs.450 crore Delhi fenestration quote, and a Rs.225 crore Raidurg bid.
Management says it is choosing jobs on client, terms, margin and execution period rather than chasing win ratio, and that it could win all Rs.3,000 crores of pipeline by cutting prices about 5%.

Q2 wins included a Mumbai hotel job of about Rs.90 crores and two South India data-centre jobs of about Rs.35-40 crores. Management expects data centres to be a few jobs only, with hospitality and commercial as stronger segments.

Pass-through clauses cover aluminium and glass. Claims are certified in 45-60 days, and management says this makes the company risk-free from commodity moves on current projects. Management says none of the jobs are cost-plus; all are re-measurable item-rate contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Are US customers cancelling existing orders, or is the Q3-Q4 strength tied to new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing orders are funded and dispatching daily, so none are being stopped. The slowdown relates to new US jobs, which developers are holding until prices normalise. Management expects a pent-up wave of awards after the US midterms or an end to the war.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp Q2 margin increase on flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to Rs.6 crores of escalation claims booked in Q2 for costs incurred in Q1, and to a richer mix from fenestration. It reiterated FY27 guidance of 23-25% EBITDA and 18-20% PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.500 crores order target for Q3-Q4 alone, and what is the split across segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is for Q3-Q4 only and said bookings will come from all three segments, without giving a split.

qa_highlights.question: How do aluminium and glass price changes flow through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through claims are raised after the client-side base rate is reconciled, and are paid 45-60 days after cost is incurred. It said the company carries no commodity risk on current projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-22% growth guidance net of freight, and what is the freight mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is net of freight, which is a pass-through. The CFO said the company receives an advance against freight, so there is no new working-capital blockage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Israel and US new-client wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a first Israel order in Q3-Q4 FY27, initially below Rs.50 crores, with larger jobs possible within 1.5-2 years. It said the US bids cover both existing and new clients, with a couple of awards possible in the next quarter.

risks_watch: International revenue fell 14% in H1, and Q3-Q4 depends on US and Israel awards that management has not yet booked.
Q2 margin spike was partly due to escalation-claim timing; management itself said margins could move up and down.
H2 revenue depends on converting about Rs.500 crores of bookings in two quarters; no split was given.
Glass processing unit timeline is July-August 2027, and the margin benefit is estimated at 1-1.5%.
Some domestic projects are behind schedule on the client side.
Working capital is currently negative at -19 days, against a stated normalised level of about 45 days.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on domestic demand, fenestration and the Q3-Q4 ramp. Noticeably evasive on the US and international order timing, on the Q2 margin spike and on the Rs.500 crores booking split, which management declined to break out.
key_quotes: So, I see no reason to change any sort of guidance for this year and even for the next year.
If I were to drop my prices by 5%, I would get all of the Rs. 3,000 crores orders tomorrow itself.
None of our jobs are cost-plus. All our jobs are re-measurable item rate contracts.

adds.what: Glass processing unit (cost about Rs.70-odd crores, IPO-funded)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-22% (midpoint 21%) with margins held; backed by a Rs.957 crore order book and a Rs.500 crore-plus Q3-Q4 bookings target, but the glass processing unit only starts around July-August 2027 and the call gives no capacity additions needed for the guided growth.
